findings.tariffChannel: Powy Charge app / direct QR payment / RFID
positiveEvidence: Current first-party Powy site identifies Powy as a brand of TheF Charging S.r.l., resolving the commercial-name alias without creating a second CPO.
Current first-party FAQ states charging costs vary according to charging-point power and charging duration and are shown in Powy Charge before starting.
Current first-party direct-payment page allows app-less charging by QR/code and states selected stations can expose promotional rates; therefore point-specific tariff capture is required.
negativePaths: Do not infer one network-wide Powy/TheF price from third-party eMSP tables.
Do not count Powy as a separate canonical CPO from TheF Charging partyId PWY.
Do not promote a station tariff to all PWY EVSE because first-party documentation explicitly allows variation by power/duration and selected-station promotions.
findings.blockage: exact current direct tariff components are exposed at the selected point/session rather than as one deterministic public network tariff
findings.resumeCondition: crawl Powy Charge/direct-payment QR backend for IT*PWY EVSE and persist exact energy/time/start/occupancy components plus validity; fail-close unmatched EVSE

findings.tariffModel: native app current-value pricing with subscription discounts; roaming separately point-priced
findings.tariffChannel: AGSM AIM E-MOBILITY app / native AGSM AIM stations; roaming separated
positiveEvidence: Current 2026 first-party terms state subscription commercial value and included energy are displayed in the app at purchase time.
Fast Flat costs 10 EUR and grants a 10% discount on the Fast charging tariff, only on AGSM AIM-owned stations.
Roaming is explicitly separated and the transaction price is shown on the selected connector activation screen.
Current terms define an occupancy penalty of 0.12 EUR/min after the allowed post-charge window for AC up to 22 kW during 07:00-23:00; other connector/time rules remain document/app-specific.
negativePaths: Do not reuse 2023/2024 package or pay-per-use prices as current September 2026 energy tariffs without current app evidence.
Do not treat AGSM AIM eMSP roaming prices as direct CPO prices.
Do not infer the underlying Fast tariff from the 10% Fast Flat discount alone.
findings.blockage: current direct energy price(s) are not enumerated in the public 2026 terms and are exposed dynamically in the app
findings.resumeCondition: capture current AGSM AIM E-MOBILITY native connector payload for IT*ASS EVSE, preserving base energy tariff, subscription eligibility and occupancy penalty; fail-close unmatched EVSE

findings.tariffModel: NextCharge-connected station-specific pricing / host-managed CPO infrastructure
findings.tariffChannel: DriWe Charge infrastructure surfaced through NextCharge; Unoenergy/DriWe native ecosystem
positiveEvidence: Current DriWe first-party App & Card page states DriWe Charge stations are geolocated on the NextCharge app and station/session information is accessed through that platform.
Unoenergy confirms it acquired DriWe and identifies DriWe as a Charging Point Operator and technology integrator.
Current Unoenergy charging pages expose the DriWe map as the place to visualize, book and pay rather than publishing one retail network tariff.
negativePaths: Do not infer a DriWe network-wide direct tariff from generic NextCharge eMSP prices.
Do not assume Unoenergy domestic wallbox pricing has any relationship to public DRW charging tariffs.
findings.blockage: no current first-party deterministic network tariff is published; retail price must be joined at station/EVSE level from the connected platform/native point
findings.resumeCondition: bulk join IT*DRW EVSE to NextCharge/native DriWe station payload and retain exact current direct/eMSP channel distinction and price components; fail-close unmatched EVSE
